My family has worked this land for generations. Here in Quzhou, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize — that's the rotation. The land is flat, we have wells for irrigation, and there's a grain buyer who comes through the village. I don't think about doing anything different. My husband goes to the city for work most of the year, so I handle the fields myself with help from my mother-in-law during busy periods.

I have about 10 mu of flat dryland. After the wheat comes off in June, I turn around and put the maize in the same fields. That's how we do it here — two crops on the same land each year.

For wheat, I buy the improved seed from the village cooperative — they carry Jimai varieties, which do well here. I don't know how to select seed myself, so I trust what they sell. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: before winter to help rooting, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading. Less than three times and I worry the yield drops. I spray twice — once for aphids and once for rust, which hits us most years.

For maize, everyone buys hybrid seed. The salesman at the supply store says Zhengdan 958 is reliable and I've used it before with good results. I put urea down in two splits. Summer gets rain so I only irrigate once if July is dry. After wheat harvest I seed directly into the stubble — no time for deep ploughing in summer, and my neighbor says it's fine.
